hidden_cause: The body of the P1 branch triple-duty (balancing/check) valve, between the P1 branch isolation valves, has corroded through and is leaking; with the fill valve closed, the loop bled down until P1 air-bound and the chiller tripped on low evaporator flow.

key_evidence: P1 shows running while chilled-water flow is near zero: a run status proves the motor turns, not that water moves.
The chiller panel shows LowEvapFlow, and that diagnostic is not on the BAS.
The suction gauge reads far below fill pressure; there is no BAS point for loop pressure.
P1 draws well under nameplate amps: an air-bound pump unloads.
Standing water spreads from the P1 branch.
safe_path: De-energize P1, or escalate, before going hands-on near it in standing water.
Isolate the P1 branch to stop the leak, then replace the valve body.
Refill, close the fill valve again, and vent the air.
Restore a pump, confirm flow, then reset the chiller once.
Watch the supply temperature settle while the loop holds pressure with the fill closed.
traps: Refilling with the fill valve left open holds pressure while the floor keeps flooding.
Resetting the chiller without flow re-trips it.
The strainer and MAU04 read normal.
